text: Linear Algebra I: Practice Midterm Solution October 10, 2025 Problem 1. Suppose W is a subspace of V and v1 + W, . . . , vm + W is a basis of V /W . Let w1, . . . , wn be a basis of W . Show that v1, . . . , vm, w1, . . . , wn is a basis of V . Proof. We show that v1, . . . , vm, w1, . . . , wn is a basis of V . Spanning: Let v ∈ V . Since v1 + W, . . . , vm + W is a basis of V /W , v + W = a1(v1 + W ) + · · · + am(vm + W ) for some a1, . . . , am ∈ F . Then v − (a1v1 + · · · + amvm) ∈ W. Let u = v − (a1v1 + · · · + amvm) ∈ W . Since w1, . . . , wn is a basis of W , u = b1w1 + · · · + bnwn for some bj ∈ F . Thus v = a1v1 + · · · + amvm + b1w1 + · · · + bnwn. So the set spans V . Linear independence: Suppose a1v1 + · · · + amvm + b1w1 + · · · + bnwn = 0. Rewriting: a1v1 + · · · + amvm = −(b1w1 + · · · + bnwn) ∈ W. Then in V /W , a1(v1 + W ) + · · · + am(vm + W ) = 0 + W. Since v1 + W, . . . , vm + W are linearly independent in V /W , a1 = · · · = am = 0. Then b1w1 + · · · + bnwn = 0, and since w1, . . . , wn is a basis of W , b1 = · · · = bn = 0. So the set is linearly independent. Hence v1, . . . , vm, w1, . . . , wn is a basis of V . 1 Problem 2. Let V be a finite dimensional vector space. Let φ ∈ V ∗ be nonzero. Show that there exists v ∈ V with φ(v) = 1 and V = span{v} ⊕ ker φ. Proof. Since φ ̸= 0, pick u ∈ V with φ(u) ̸= 0. Define v = u φ(u) . Then φ(v) = 1. Now, for any x ∈ V , write x = φ(x)v + (x − φ(x)v). We have φ(x)v ∈ span{v}, and φ (x − φ(x)v) = φ(x) − φ(x) · 1 = 0, so x − φ(x)v ∈ ker φ. Hence V = span{v} + ker φ. To show the sum is direct: suppose av ∈ span{v} ∩ ker φ. Then φ(av) = a = 0, so a = 0. Thus the intersection is trivial. Therefore V = span{v} ⊕ ker φ. 2 Problem 3. Let V be the subspace of C(R) given by span(e3x cos x, e3x sin x). Consider the linear map L : V → C(R) defined by L(f ) = f ′ − f , where the prime denotes differentiation with respect to x. (i) Show that e3x cos x, e3x sin x are linearly independent. (ii) Show that the image of L is in V , that is im L ⊂ V . (iii) Let β = (e3x cos x, e3x sin x), find [L]β β. (iv) Find ker L and im L. (v) Find a solution to the differential equation f ′ − f = 2e3x cos x. Proof. (i) Suppose ae3x cos x + be3x sin x = 0 for all x. Dividing by e3x, we get a cos x + b sin x = 0. Let x = 0 we have a = 0. Let x = π/2 we have b = 0. So they are linearly independent. (ii) Let f = Ae3x cos x + Be3x sin x. Then f ′ = e 3x[(3A + B) cos x + (−A + 3B) sin x]. So L(f ) = f ′ − f = e3x[(2A + B) cos x + (−A + 2B) sin x] ∈ V. (iii) Let u1 = e3x cos x, u2 = e3x sin x. By the formula in (ii) we have L(u1) = 2u1 − u2, L(u2) = u1 + 2u2. So [L] β β = ( 2 1 −1 2 ) . (iv) Let f = Ae3x cos x + Be3x sin x ∈ V . And suppose L(f ) = e3x [(2A + B) cos x + (−A + 2B) sin x = 0] . Hence by linear independence 2A + B = 0, −A + 2B = 0. From the first, B = −2A. Sub into second: −A − 4A = −5A = 0 ⇒ A = 0 ⇒ B = 0. So ker L = {0}. Since L : V → V is linear and injective, we know from class it is surjective and we have im L = V .
